name: small-change
description: Small bounded change workflow: analyze, choose an optimal approach, update existing models for the change and its neighbors, then specify with failing tests and implement in small iterations.

jobs.prompt:
Triage the work. Two entry paths:

1. A GitHub board item was provided or is implied: pull it from the project's default board.
2. The user gave qualitative text describing a small change: first run /backlog to create the item on the board, then treat the newly created item as the ticket.

Immediately decide: is this a small, bounded change? Do not do any further work before making this call.

- NOT a small change (large feature, multi-module rewrite, or unclear): tell the parent you cannot continue and stop. Do not run start-ticket. Do not analyze.
- IS a small change: run /start-ticket immediately to create the branch and session before doing anything else. Do not bind or rely on a durable CliAgent work session on main before start-ticket - a leftover ``default`` (or folder-slug) session is the wrong bind. After start-ticket completes, rebind workspace root to the ticket worktree (``rebind_to_worktree``) on ``session/<ticket>``. The same session==branch==worktree isolation and post-start-ticket rebind must hold for CliAgent, SubAgent, and no-agent flows - not only CLI spawn. Then stop this job; analysis is next.

The ticket is confirmed as a small change and start-ticket has already been run. Now analyze the change - do not hunt for defects or problems.

- Read all context files (.context/, module-context.md, grill-answers).
- Analyze repo history for the area of the change.
- Search for similar past changes and related tickets.
- Map the current behavior and the intended delta. Be thorough about the change surface - do not stop at the first file that looks related.

Add your full analysis to the ticket notes under ## Analysis (separated from existing content).
jobs.judge_criteria: PASS only when: (1) context was read in full; (2) repo history and similar past changes were explored; (3) the write-up is about the intended change, not a defect hunt; (4) analysis was added to the ticket notes under ## Analysis.

jobs.prompt:
Determine the optimal approach for this small change.  you are choosing how to make the change with the least disruption.

Consider at least two plausible approaches. Pick one and say why it is better (smaller seam, existing patterns, fewer modules touched, safer rollback).

Critical distinction - make this explicit in the approach:
- PROMPT/AI CHANGE: the change is to instructions, prompts, rules, or agent behaviour - not production code.
- CODE CHANGE: the change is a production-code edit.
- BOTH: the change needs both.

State clearly which category applies. Category informs emphasis in the always-required mechanical and agentic BDD suites; it does not waive either suite.

Add the chosen approach, rejected alternatives, and category to the ticket notes under ## Approach (separated from the analysis above).
jobs.judge_criteria: PASS only when: (1) at least two plausible approaches were considered; (2) one concrete approach is chosen with a reason; (3) the category (prompt/AI change vs code change vs both) is explicitly stated; (4) the chosen approach, rejected alternatives, and category are in the ticket notes under ## Approach.

jobs.prompt:
Document the small change in existing models - do not model the whole area from scratch.

The listed items are context tools, not actions. Doer action is generate. Judge action is validate against what the doer generated.

Use CleanEngineering generate at model fidelity (/clean_engineering.model) and Bdd generate at behavior fidelity (/bdd.behavior).

Rules:
- If a clean-engineering model or module-context already exists for the touched module(s): alter it in place. Do not generate a new model of the entire module or of every module that might be impacted.
- If a BDD behavior spec already exists for the subject: alter the existing describe/it hierarchy. Add or change only the examples that cover this change and the immediately surrounding pieces that must stay consistent.
- If no model or behavior spec exists for the exact change surface: create the thinnest new artifact that covers the change and its neighbors - not a full-surface model of the parent area.
- Scope is the change plus surrounding pieces that callers of the changed seam will see. Do not document the whole impacted area, every public method on the module, or unrelated siblings.
- Record what you altered vs what you left alone under ## Model on the ticket notes.

Do not implement tests or production code in this job - model/context and behavior signatures only.
jobs.judge_criteria: The judge has the same listed tools. Doer used generate; judge uses validate (and scan) against what was generated - CleanEngineering at model fidelity and Bdd at behavior fidelity. PASS only when: (1) existing models and behavior specs in the change area were found and read, or their absence was documented; (2) existing artifacts were altered in place rather than rewritten from scratch (thin new artifacts only when none existed); (3) scope is the change plus immediately surrounding pieces - not a full remodel of the impacted area; (4) generate was used on those tools; (5) what was altered vs left alone is recorded under ## Model on the ticket; (6) the judge ran validate against the generated artifacts with those tools and both passed.

jobs.prompt:
Write failing tests for the intended small change before writing any implementation. Orchestrate the most robust testing you can: always use both mechanical BDD and agentic BDD - prefer over-testing to missing a hole.

The listed items are context tools, not actions. Doer action is generate. Judge action is validate against what the doer generated.

- Mechanical (vanilla) BDD via Bdd generate at development fidelity (/bdd.development) - required.
- Agentic BDD via AgentBdd generate at development fidelity (/agent-bdd.development) - required. Exercise the real agent/CLI harness path; do not treat a stubbed or patched-out pickup/spawn path as sufficient agentic coverage.
- Run mechanical BDD first, then agentic BDD.
- Approach category (prompt/AI vs code vs both) still informs what each suite emphasizes; it does not waive either suite.

The failing tests are a hard requirement - write them first, run them, confirm they fail (red) for the new behavior. You may alter existing tests or add new ones, but explicit red mechanical and agentic tests capturing the intended change must exist before any implementation is written.
jobs.judge_criteria: The judge has the same listed tools. Doer used generate; judge uses validate against what was generated. PASS only when: (1) at least one failing mechanical BDD test exists that captures the intended change; (2) at least one failing agentic BDD test exists that captures the intended change via the real agent harness (not only a stubbed path); (3) mechanical BDD was run before agentic BDD; (4) the judge ran validate against those generated tests with those tools. Pre-existing, unrelated test failures are out of scope - do not fail the job because of failures that existed before this change was introduced.

jobs.prompt:
Implement the small change using CleanEngineering generate at code fidelity (/clean_engineering.code) in small iterations. Work one small piece at a time - change just enough to make one or a few tests pass, then move to the next piece. Repeat until all mechanical BDD and agentic BDD tests are green. Always run vanilla BDD first, then agentic BDD. Both suites are required; do not stop when only mechanical is green.

The listed items are context tools, not actions. Doer action is generate. Judge action is validate against what the doer generated.

Follow the approach recorded under ## Approach. Do not expand scope beyond that approach.

Before writing any code:
- Explore the impacted modules and the code they depend on - only as far as the change and surrounding pieces require.
- Read module-context.md for every module you touch.
- Study the existing idioms, patterns, and usage in detail. Do not invent new patterns or paradigms - follow what is already there. A small change should not require new patterns.

When this item's small-change jobs are complete: call finish-ticket before next_backlog_item.
jobs.judge_criteria: The judge has the same listed tools. Doer used generate; judge uses validate against what was generated. PASS only when: (1) all mechanical BDD tests written for this change pass; (2) all agentic BDD tests written for this change pass; (3) the implementation follows the recorded ## Approach and existing patterns - no new patterns invented without strong justification; (4) the judge ran validate against the generated code and tests with those tools. Pre-existing, unrelated test failures are out of scope - judge only the tests introduced or changed for this item, not the full suite baseline.
